newsitem.title: UK: UK Spitsbergen licensed to build Indonesia refinery.
newsitem.headline: UK Spitsbergen licensed to build Indonesia refinery.

text.p: Britain's Spitsbergen Oil and Gas and a private Indonesian partner are looking to finance a $1 billion refinery project in central-south Java after receiving a licence from the Indonesian government, Spitsbergen said on Monday.
Little-known Spitsbergen, a privately held company based in Kent, southern England, said it was in negotiations with two unnamed Western oil majors on the project.

The company was issued the licence in partnership with private Indonesian firm PT Felima Orient Pacific in a joint venture called SOG Indonesia. Spitsbergen holds 85 percent equity in the venture, Felima 15 percent.
As many as a dozen licences are believed to have been issued for potential refinery projects in Indonesia, though no more than two or three are likely to proceed, industry sources said.
Spitsbergen said Felima boasted an "extremely close" relationship with Indonesian state oil company Pertamina and the Indonesian government.

"The refinery will cost $1 billion in the initial phase, but it could be as much as $2.5-2.7 billion over six years if full petchem units are included," said Spitsbergen's operations director Crispin Naismith.
Jakarta recently issued new guidelines clearing the way for private sector companies to build and operate refineries in the archipelago.
